The Phase 1 cough ceiling row now cites CORAL (60.2% relative reduction vs 16.9% placebo at 6 weeks) and CANAL alongside PACIFY COUGH. The other eleven entities (AK3280, EZ-2053, HEC585, HSK44459, TDI01, minocycline, azathioprine monotherapy, lansoprazole, sodium pyruvate, methylprednisolone/prednisone monotherapy, and the doxycycline label) returned no IPF randomised report and stay 'Poorly studied'.

Phase 4 must not treat any of these six as an evidence gap. Establishes that the Phase 2 per-entity search under-retrieves for agents whose registry label is a code name or a two-drug string; the residual 208 'Poorly studied' rows are therefore an upper bound on genuine absence of evidence.

The cough question has a randomised answer.

claim_corrected: Phase 2 graded bexotegrast as a positive randomised signal below phase 3 (later corrected in C16 to a non-clinical primary endpoint) and Phase 3 listed it among small programmes awaiting adequately sized follow-up (M6.11).
correction: Bexotegrast is reclassified as 'Harm outweighs benefit'. In BEACON-IPF (NCT06097260, n=319 randomised), terminated on DSMB recommendation, registry-posted results show more disease-progression events on bexotegrast than placebo: 5 of 106 (placebo), 16 of 105 (160 mg) and 25 of 108 (320 mg); Cox hazard ratios versus placebo 3.31 (95% CI 1.21-9.05, p=0.0194) and 5.36 (95% CI 2.05-13.99, p=0.0006). A >=10% absolute FVC decline was also more frequent (odds ratio 3.33, 95% CI 1.03-10.81, p=0.0449 for 160 mg; 3.01, 95% CI 0.91-9.91, p=0.07 for 320 mg). Deaths: 0 of 106, 6 of 105 and 4 of 108; serious adverse events 6, 17 and 21. The week-52 FVC primary endpoint is uninformative because only 1, 1 and 2 participants reached week 52 after early termination.
basis: ClinicalTrials.gov results section for NCT06097260, retrieved 2026-09-03. The Phase 2 search used PubMed only and no peer-reviewed publication of these results was identified, so a registry-results check was required to find them.
effect: Landscape verdict changed Uncertain->Harm outweighs benefit; negative-results register row reclassified to the harm domain; new map statement M2.15; bexotegrast removed from M6.11; candidate P27 rejected as superseded by its own trial. claim_corrected: The traditional-medicine screen was described as resting on English-indexed records, with the size of the missing Chinese-language literature unknown.
correction: The gap is now quantified from English-indexed systematic reviews that pooled Chinese-database trials: 63 randomised trials of Chinese medicine injections (PMID 35881610), 20 trials in 1363 patients across four injection products (PMID 36451506), 23 trials in 1390 patients of qi-supplementing and blood-activating herbs (PMID 35245333), 11 trials in 981 patients of external TCM treatment (PMID 41088620), a Chinese-herb-versus-N-acetylcysteine comparison in 733 patients (PMID 31312224), and an overview of reviews covering 15550 participants (PMID 37235494). Not one Chinese medicine injection product appears in the landscape, and the herbal-versus-N-acetylcysteine comparison is absent from the record. These reviews are secondary sources and their own quality statements are cautionary (limited number and quality of included studies), so no verdict is assigned to any of this evidence here.
basis: PubMed searches for Chinese herbal medicine, TCM injections, acupuncture and exercise interventions in IPF; abstracts of the six reviews listed; register ipf_phase6_chinese_language_coverage.csv. ClinicalTrials.gov mirror not applicable - these trials are registered in ChiCTR or unregistered.
effect: New map row M5.14; new limitation L7; retrieval action A12 opened. The landscape's 'Poorly studied' count remains an upper bound on genuine absence of evidence, and this correction identifies where the largest single block of unexamined randomised evidence sits.

claim_corrected: Kangxian Huanji Granule (PMID 37993378) was graded from a partial abstract, with the trial design not established.
correction: The full structured abstract is retrieved: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled exploratory trial, n=80, 10 g twice daily for 4 weeks added to conventional treatment in acute exacerbation of IPF, followed 12 weeks, registered as ChiCTR1900026289. Co-primary endpoints were treatment failure and all-cause mortality: treatment failure at 4 weeks RR 0.22 (95% CI 0.051-0.965, P=0.023); all-cause mortality at 16 weeks RR 0.75 (95% CI 0.179-3.138, P>0.999); acute exacerbation rate RR 0.69 (95% CI 0.334-1.434, P=0.317); length of hospitalisation -3.30 days (95% CI -6.300 to -0.300, P=0.032); mMRC -0.67 (95% CI -0.89 to -0.44, P<0.001) and SGRQ-I -10.36 (95% CI -16.483 to -4.228, P=0.001) at 4 weeks.
basis: Publisher abstract for doi 10.1016/j.joim.2023.11.003 retrieved via DOI resolution; full text remains closed access with no open-access or PubMed Central copy.
effect: Candidate P17 stays held at verification (screen S5): the design is now known but the full text, the ChiCTR record and any independent replication are still unavailable. The verdict remains Uncertain; the mortality endpoint is null and only the treatment-failure endpoint is positive, so the trial is not evidence of a survival effect.

claim_corrected: Full text of PMID 26331942 (TOLLIP x N-acetylcysteine interaction) was recorded as unobtainable.
correction: The PubMed Central deposit was retrieved but contains front matter and the abstract only (the article is closed access with no body text). The record's quoted values are now confirmed against the primary abstract: interaction P=0.001 for rs3750920; composite-endpoint hazard ratio 0.14 (95% CI 0.02-0.83, P=0.03) in TT patients and 3.23 (95% CI 0.79-13.16, P=0.10) in CC patients, with replication in an independent cohort and an explicit author call for a genotype-stratified prospective trial before any off-label recommendation.
basis: PubMed Central deposit for doi 10.1164/rccm.201505-1010OC (4.5 kB, abstract only); PubMed abstract.
effect: Candidate P10 stays unpromoted, but its reason changes: the numbers are verified, while the genotype subgroup sizes, whether the interaction was prespecified, and the replication cohort's composition remain unverifiable without publisher access. The genotype-stratified trial the authors asked for exists and is complete but unreported (PRECISIONS, action A1), so the smallest next step is retrieval, not a new trial.

basis: ipf_phase2_landscape.csv verdict tallies after actions A3 and A4; PubMed NCT-indexed searches for the 110 completed trials with no retrievable results.
effect: Supersedes the counts in C31 and C33. Action A3 also established that better searching recovers very little: of 110 completed trials with no retrievable results, only 7 had any indexed publication and none of those reported the missing primary clinical outcome, so the deficit is genuine non-reporting rather than a search failure.
